content: Clalit, one of Israel's leading health maintenance organizations (HMOs), was established in 1911 by a group of 150 immigrants who sought to create a mutual aid healthcare association. When the State of Israel was founded in 1948, Clalit played a pivotal role in restructuring the nation's healthcare system to accommodate the influx of new immigrants. Today, Clalit operates clinics in nearly every neighborhood across the country. In January 1995, Israel implemented its national health insurance law, establishing a mandatory healthcare system supported by four service providers: Clalit, Leumit, Maccabi, and Meuhedet. Clalit is the largest of these providers, insuring approximately 3.8 million members, which accounts for 60% of Israel's population. Clalit manages its own network of hospitals throughout the country, comprising 14 hospitals, including psychiatric and rehabilitation facilities, all of which are affiliated with universities. Additionally, Clalit operates 1,200 primary and specialized clinics, as well as a network of pharmacies and dental clinics. Clalit oversees several prominent hospitals, each with specialized areas of expertise: Rabin Medical Center – Beilinson Campus (established in 1938) in Petah Tikva specializes in open-heart surgery, neurosurgery, and organ transplants, including heart, liver, and kidney transplants. Rabin Medical Center – Golda Campus (established in 1942) in Petah Tikva focuses on total joint replacement, home dialysis, vascular surgery, and hematology research utilizing electron microscopy. Lady Davis Hospital (established in 1967) in Haifa is part of the Carmel Medical Center and serves the diverse population of Haifa and its surrounding areas. Its specialties include cardiology, cardiovascular and thoracic surgery, and community medicine epidemiology. HaEmek Hospital (established in 1930) in Afula is part of the HaEmek Valley Medical Center and specializes in treating fertility and reproductive health issues. Meir Hospital (established in 1960) in Kfar Saba is part of the Sapir Medical Center and is renowned for its expertise in pulmonary diseases and spinal surgery. Kaplan Medical Center (established in 1953) in Rehovot is recognized for its proficiency in hand surgery. Soroka Hospital (established in 1960) in Beersheba serves as the primary hospital for the Negev region. Yoseftal Hospital (established in 1968) in Eilat is part of the Yoseftal Medical Center and is Israel’s southernmost hospital. Despite its extensive contributions to healthcare, Clalit-run hospitals have faced criticism. In March 2007, Professor Gabi Barabash, the director of Tel Aviv's Ichilov Hospital, criticized the Israeli Health Ministry for permitting Clalit to operate private hospitals. He argued that this practice could have detrimental effects on the public hospitalization system. Similarly, Ruth Ralbag, a senior official in the Health Ministry's budget department, expressed concerns that the incentives for establishing private hospitals could weaken the public health system and exacerbate socioeconomic disparities among healthcare consumers.
